reason: Full-width caption band across the /worlds hero map's bottom edge — a photo-credit bar on the page's dominant element, not a layout box competing for page space. The band's job is to label the map; it does not push content down or spend page area. Named in globals.css next to the rule.

A two-up switcher band: each tab spans its 1fr column of a two-column grid, the way a search field spans its row. The defect this class carried — min-height 112px against 65px of content — was removed on 15 November (65px measured). The width is the named composition, not an inflation.

The hero map is the /worlds page's dominant element and its own image; the linter counts its canvas/img as a tall empty box and its compass glyphs (arrow, north mark) as emoji. Those are the map and required symbols, not decoration.

Named register: /worlds is the marketing surface for the generated Minecraft worlds, and its dark ground is the product's own identity (mean luminance measured 55-62, single amber accent, glow 0, shadows 0, pills 5, radius 0). The rule's other triggers — glow, glass, pills — measure zero; what fires it is 'dark' plus 2 gradients, both of them the 12%-opacity hero grid pattern and the dark legibility shade over the hero photo, which the zero-gradient law explicitly allows.

Pixel-derived: the largest flat region (measured 0.40-0.43) is the hero map image's own ground. The map IS the payload of this page (mapShareFirstScreen measures it under 0.4 only because the metric requires a live map container, and this hero is a rendered image by design — an interactive product page).
